Residual correlation terms are not supported in a nonlinear (nl = TRUE) formula; 'ar()' appears in the model body, where it would be evaluated as ordinary R code rather than read as a term. brms reaches the same model through acformula(), which has no analog here

quadrature = TRUE cannot be combined with the residual correlation term ar(week, subj, cov = TRUE): the rule integrates a random effect against per-observation densities, and this residual is a joint density over each group. Use quadrature = FALSE (Laplace) or REML = TRUE

residuals(type = \osa\") is not available for a fit with a residual correlation term (ar(week, subj, cov = TRUE)): the likelihood is a joint density per group, not a product of per-observation terms. Use type = \"pearson\", which divides by the marginal residual SD, or dharma_residuals(), which uses si"

cosy(): time points within groups must be unique; group '1' has 4 rows at time '1'. The first argument of cosy() is the TIME variable and the second is the grouping variable, so cosy(g) reads g as time; write cosy(gr = g) if g is the group.
unstr() needs both a time variable and a grouping variable: unstr(week, subj)
ar(): the residual correlation needs at least 2 time points; 'one' gives 1
ar(): 400 time points would build a dense 400 x 400 residual covariance on every gradient evaluation (cap 300). Name a grouping variable - ar(t, gr = subject) - so the density factorizes over groups
unstr(): 60 time points means 1770 free correlations (cap 50 levels). Use ar(), arma() or cosy() for a structure that does not grow with the number of time points
An autocorrelation term cannot be crossed with ':': x:ar(week, subj, cov = TRUE). Write it as a separate term: y ~ ... + ar(...)
